Feature: Is there an overt marker for the absolutive?
curated_comment: changed to 0.. An overt clitic =i exists, but it marks the UNDERGOER macrorole (P and patientive S), not a canonical absolutive: agentive S is zero-marked (ex.3b). In a split-intransitive system this is an undergoer/objective marker, so the 'absolutive' label is approximate. If Ergon reserves 'absolutive' for ergative-absolutive systems, reconsider as 0/N-A. Arka 2012:153.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on first person pronouns?
curated_comment: CORRECTED 1->0. Marori has NO ergative flagging. =i marks the UNDERGOER macrorole only (Patient/Object and patientive S); A and agentive S are zero-marked (Arka 2012:153: ex.1b Nawa[A, bare] payung=i[P]; ex.3a Na=i 'I suffered cold' [patientive S] vs ex.3b Efi '(*=i)' ran [agentive S, bare]). Because S is split (Sp patterns with P, Sa with A), the alignment is split-intransitive/active, not ergative. A is never flagged. The 1st-person token na=i flags an undergoer, not an ergative A. Coding 0.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on second person pronouns?
curated_comment: CORRECTED 1->0. Same basis as GB409_2. =i flags undergoers (P and patientive S), never A or agentive S; S is split, so the system is active/split-intransitive, not ergative. No ergative flag exists on any 2nd-person form. Coding 0.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on third person pronouns?
curated_comment: CORRECTED 1->0. Same basis. 3rd-person U arguments (Albert=i, Robertus=i, Maria=i) carry the undergoer clitic =i, while 3rd-person A (Efi purfam 'that person', ex.5b) is zero-marked. =i is an undergoer marker, not an ergative flag; with split S the alignment is active, not ergative. Coding 0.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on full NPs?
curated_comment: CORRECTED 1->0. Full-NP A is zero-marked (ex.5b Efi purfam [A], bare); full-NP P/recipient takes =i (Albert=i, Robertus=i, Maria=i). The curator's cited ex.1a (Ka ku=ndo, intransitive) actually shows a bare agentive S. With split S (Sp=i, Sa bare) the system is split-intransitive/active, not ergative. No ergative flagging on full NPs. Coding 0.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the imperfective aspect?
curated_comment: Set to 0 (Marori is non-ergative). The clitic =i marks the UNDERGOER macrorole (Patient/Object and patientive S) in a split-intransitive/active system; A and agentive S are always zero-marked, so there is no ergative flagging anywhere. Ergative alignment is absent from the language and therefore absent in the imperfective aspect. See GB409_2-5; Arka 2012:153-154.

Feature: Is ergative alignment of flagging conditioned by any other factor?
Comment: The patientive S of motion predicate do not receives =i, instead, receives suffix agreement.
curated_comment: CORRECTED 1->0. There is no ergative alignment for any factor to condition. The split-intransitivity that conditions the UNDERGOER marker =i (patientive S of state verbs takes =i, ex.3a; patientive S of motion verbs takes suffix agreement instead, ex.4; agentive S is bare, ex.3b) is a property of undergoer marking, not of ergative alignment. See GB409_2-5. Coding 0.

Feature: Are the ergative and the genitive expressed by the same marker?
curated_comment: 0. No distinct ergative marker exists in Marori (A and agentive S are zero-marked; =i is an undergoer marker), so ergative=genitive syncretism is not applicable. Arka 2012:152-154.
